purpose: Compare response error and candidate-selection loss using identical held-out source panels; test implementation and support before final analysis.
training_policy: Small candidate/condition count does not invalidate otherwise verified training rows. Expanded training additionally permits Wang2021 pH rows with source-supported condition mappings and explicitly unverified figure-derived responses. No unresolved isotherm rows enter.
external_sources: Kim2019 is test-only; its responses never enter training for any fold.
test_policy: Common-condition complete grids within each source and experimental series; all rows of held-out candidates excluded from training, including unscored incomplete grids.
model_selection: Fixed parameters for this development pilot; no model or feature selection using test loss. Final tuned analysis remains separate.
feature_policy: CEC omitted from all full models because it is not available for Kim2019; source identifiers and final concentration never enter features. Unreported matrix is explicitly labeled, not inferred to be pure water.
response: reported experimental adsorption capacity converted to mg/g by pollutant; no fitted qmax
scaling: Numeric predictors and response standardized using training rows only; constant fields left constant. Row-weighted fitting.
primary_loss: max observed capacity minus expected observed capacity of uniformly selected prediction maximizers
baseline: Uniform candidate selection within the identical condition; expected loss computed exactly
ties: Prediction tie absolute tolerance 1e-12; observed ties use recorded values. This is not experimental uncertainty.
aggregation: First mean conditions within series; mean series within source; never count multiple series as independent studies. Report pollutant tasks separately.
known_limits: Few sources, buffer and dose shift, compilation rather than independent original response replication, unknown experimental uncertainty; this pilot alone is not the completed research objective. Cui source-family sensitivity and broader data review remain required.
